cases.rationale: Easy single-phase CaWO4 control with the exact scheelite reference available. Zero offset and specimen effects are controlled, leaving only the ordinary reference mismatch and counting statistics; it tests whether routine search, project construction, and profile refinement work before multiphase or missing-reference complications.

Low-count partial ZnO + WO3 reaction with full references: 72 wt% ZnWO4 plus stoichiometrically paired residual monoclinic WO3 and 7.3 wt% ZnO. It tests complete minor-phase inventory, overlapping multiphase fitting, and persistence when the weakest known phase is easy to omit.

Partial SrCO3 + WO3 reaction containing SrWO4, residual carbonate, and residual monoclinic WO3 at mass-balanced fractions. All SrWO4 entries are withheld; the nearest surviving framework is tier-1 CaWO4 (COD 7219229, Ca->Sr, framework RMS 0.0226, 4.3% cell mismatch). This tests analogue adaptation inside a three-phase carbonate-derived pattern rather than as an isolated phase.

Partial mixed-valence Mn3O4 + WO3 reaction with major MnWO4 and stoichiometric residual Mn3O4/WO3. All MnWO4 entries are withheld; the nearest survivor is tier-1 ZnWO4 (COD 1520641, Zn->Mn, framework RMS 0.0171, 2.08% cell mismatch). It combines missing wolframite recovery with a weak mixed-valence precursor phase and specimen/profile nuisance effects.

CaO + WO3 product dominated by CaWO4 but with a 10.7 wt% Ca3WO6 Ca-rich ordered intermediate and compensating WO3, preserving the overall 1:1 Ca:W dose. COD 1563081 is withheld; the nearest survivor is tier-1 Ca3OsO6 (COD 1562666, Os->W, framework RMS 0.0085, 0.38% cell mismatch). This targets recovery of a secondary off-stoichiometric phase whose strongest peaks overlap a major product and precursor.

Four-phase partial Pb3O4 + WO3 reaction/decomposition mixture with PbWO4, residual Pb3O4, orthorhombic PbO, and monoclinic WO3 at an overall 1:1 Pb:W ratio. Exact references remain available. Strong heavy-atom overlap plus a 5.4 wt% PbO component tests exhaustive phase accounting, fraction stability, and coupled profile refinement without a missing-reference confounder.
